title: Adapter protocol v1
description: A line the conformance runner and a connector's adapter exchange: a command on the adapter's stdin, or the adapter's hello, a reply or an event on its stdout. Each line is one JSON object.

hello.description: The adapter's first line, which it writes once it has loaded its connector and before it reads a command.

adapterProtocol.description: The version of the adapter protocol the adapter speaks.

name.description: The connector's name, such as node or dotnet, or baseline for the suite's plain HTTP client.

version.description: The connector's version, as its package gives it.

pid.description: The adapter's process ID, which is the connector's client process.

transports.description: The transports the connector supports on this platform.

capabilities.description: The optional capabilities the adapter offers.

command.description: A command the runner writes to the adapter's stdin. The adapter answers each one with exactly one reply.

id.description: The command's ID, which the runner gives, never reuses with the same adapter, and finds again in the reply.

oneOf.description: Calls connect() with the options, passing a cancellation signal that cancel fires. The Backend it returns is named by this command's ID.

options.description: The options, as the connector API spells them. stdin and stdout can't be inherit, since the backend would then read the runner's commands or write into the adapter's stdout.

logging.description: The level from which the adapter turns the connector's logging on, forwarding each record as a log event. Absent, the adapter turns nothing on.

sinks.description: Sinks of its own the adapter supplies for a spawned backend's output streams, in place of the options for those streams.

oneOf.description: Calls the Backend's close().
Calls the Backend's shutdown().
Reads the Backend's clientId, and the current values of the headers a request on a dialed connection carries.

Fires the cancellation signal of a call still under way: connect()'s signal, or the abort signal of a request, an SSE iteration, a typed request, dial() or a WebSocket's opening. The cancelled command still gets its reply, with whatever its call then gives. A cancel of a command whose call has ended does nothing and returns.

commandId.description: The ID of the command whose call to cancel.

oneOf.description: Sends a request through the untyped request or the Backend's primitive, writing its response as a response event and response_chunk events. The request is named by this command's ID.

headers.description: Headers the request carries beside those the connector adds.

options.description: The request's options, as the connector API spells them.

validate.description: Whether the adapter applies ValidationError to the response before reading its body. When ValidationError gives an error, the reply carries it, and the adapter reads no body.

oneOf.description: Writes a chunk of a request's streamed body. The reply comes once the adapter has handed the chunk to the body's stream.
Ends a request's streamed body.
Calls an operation of the client generated from the reference app's schema, which the adapter built on the Backend's primitive as connect() returned. It needs the typed_client capability.

operation.description: The operation's operationId in the reference app's schema.

parameters.description: The operation's path and query parameters, by the names the schema gives them.

requestBody.description: The operation's request body, as JSON, which the generated client sends in its own form.

oneOf.description: Sends a GET request through the untyped request or the primitive and iterates its response with the SSE helper, writing each event as an sse_event event. The request is named by this command's ID.

headers.description: Headers the request carries beside those the connector adds.

options.description: The request's options, as the connector API spells them.

oneOf.description: Calls the Backend's dial(), then reads the connection until it ends, writing what it reads as connection_data events. The connection is named by this command's ID.
Writes to a dialed connection.
Closes a dialed connection.
Opens a WebSocket through the path the connector's documentation gives, then writes each message it receives as a websocket_message event. The WebSocket is named by this command's ID.

headers.description: Headers the opening handshake carries beside those the connector adds.

oneOf.description: Sends a message on a WebSocket.
Starts a WebSocket's closing handshake. The reply comes once the WebSocket library's close call returns, before or after the websocket_closed event, which reports how it ended.

code.description: The close code. Absent, the close frame carries none.

reason.description: The close reason, which needs a code.

oneOf.description: Writes to the stream the Backend exposes for a piped stdin, which needs the connect command's options to set stdin to pipe.
Closes the stream the Backend exposes for a piped stdin.
Lets a stalled sink read again, from then on as a collecting sink.

reply.description: The adapter's answer to a command, written once the call the command made has returned or failed, after every event of that call.

id.description: The command's ID, or null when the adapter couldn't read a command from the line.

command.description: The command's name, as the command gave it, or null when the adapter couldn't read one.

result.description: What the call returned, as the command's result says.

oneOf.description: The call returned.
The call failed with one of the connector's errors.
The call failed with an error of the language's own.
The adapter didn't make the call.

allOf.description: A line the adapter couldn't read a command from gets a refusal.

clientId.description: The Backend's clientId once connect() returned, or null from the baseline adapter, whose plain HTTP client holds no lease.

headers.description: The headers a request on a dialed connection carries, Host, X-PipeAPI-Protocol and X-PipeAPI-Session, with the values the Backend exposes.

value.description: The value the operation returned, as JSON, or null for an operation that returns none.

event.description: What the adapter reports between replies: the progress of a call, or what a Backend or a connection did on its own.

oneOf.description: A command's call is under way: the adapter has made it, or is about to make a call that blocks until its result. The adapter writes it for every connect, request, typed_request, sse, dial and websocket_open it carries out, before the call's other events.
A lifecycle event the Backend emitted.

lifecycle.description: The event, as the connector API spells it.

oneOf.description: A record the connector logged at or above a level a connect command turned on. Its name tells which Backend logged it.

record.description: The record, as the connector API spells it, with every field the connector gave it.

message.description: The record's message, as the language's logging mechanism formats it.

oneOf.description: Output a spawned backend wrote, as a sink the adapter supplied took it: a line, from a sink that takes lines, or bytes, from one that takes bytes.
A request's response headers arrived.
A chunk of a response's body, as the adapter read it.
An event the SSE helper gave.

eventId.description: The event's ID, or null when the helper gives none.

oneOf.description: What the adapter read from a dialed connection.
A dialed connection's reading ended: the other end closed it, or reading failed with the error given.
A message the WebSocket received.
A WebSocket closed, whichever end closed it, with the code and reason its library reports, or with the error its library reported instead.

code.description: The close code the library reports.

reason.description: The close reason the library reports, which may be empty.

capability.description: An optional capability, which a case that relies on it needs the adapter's hello to declare.

oneOf.description: The connector has an Electron integration, which the adapter runs in an Electron harness.
The connector has an optional native piece, such as a Node addon, and the adapter can run it with that piece missing.
The connector checks the hello's PID against the PID of the connection's other end, on pipes and sockets, which a language's runtime may not read.
The connector opens named pipes at identification-level impersonation.
The adapter answers typed_request through a client generated from the reference app's schema.

command_id.description: A command's ID. A Backend, a request, a dialed connection or a WebSocket is named by the ID of the command that opened it.

backend.description: The Backend, named by the ID of the connect command that returned it.

request.description: The request, named by the ID of the request or sse command that sent it.

connection.description: The dialed connection, named by the ID of the dial command that opened it.

socket.description: The WebSocket, named by the ID of the websocket_open command that opened it.

client_id.description: A client ID the server gave.

oneOf.description: The connector's untyped request.
The Backend's primitive, the language's standard HTTP client set up for the backend.

target.description: The request's path and query, which the adapter passes on as they are, decoding and normalizing nothing.

headers.description: Headers in order, a name repeated for each of its values.

items.description: A header's name and one of its values.

body.description: A request's body: whole bytes, a form the language's own encoder builds, URL-encoded or multipart, or a stream the runner feeds with body_chunk and body_end.

stream.description: A streamed body, which ends with body_end.

fields.description: A form's fields in order, a name repeated for each of its values.

items.description: A field's name and one of its values.

timeout.description: The language's own timeout for the request, such as AbortSignal.timeout() or an HttpClient's Timeout, which ends it with the language's timeout error.

bytes.description: Bytes, as text when they are UTF-8, or else in base64.

text.description: The bytes, as the UTF-8 text they encode.

base64.description: The bytes, in base64 with padding.

bytes_or_line.description: Bytes, or a line of text without its line ending.

line.description: The line, without its line ending.

websocket_data.description: A WebSocket message: a text message, or a binary message in base64.

binary.description: A binary message, in base64 with padding.

stream.description: A spawned backend's output stream, as the connector API's options name it.

sink.description: A sink the adapter supplies for an output stream.

oneOf.description: A sink that takes everything at once and forwards it as output events.
A sink that takes nothing until sink_resume names its stream, then collects.

connector_error.description: One of the connector's errors, as the connector API spells it, with its code passed on as the connector carries it.

message.description: The error's message, as the language gives it.

language_error.description: An error of the language's own, which isn't one of the connector's.

oneOf.description: A cancellation signal the call took, which cancel fired.
The request's own timeout.
Any other error, such as one a WebSocket library reported.

name.description: The language's name for the error's type, such as AbortError or OperationCanceledException.

message.description: The error's message, as the language gives it.

refusal.description: Why the adapter didn't make the call a command asked for. Each is a fault of the runner or the adapter, never of the connector.

oneOf.description: The adapter doesn't know the command's name.
The adapter can't carry out the command as written, such as a line that isn't a command, a name that isn't the right kind of handle, or an option its connector doesn't take.
The adapter's own code failed, outside the call it made.

message.description: What went wrong, for the runner's report.
